newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan closes university so students go to war zone.
newsitem.headline: Sudan closes university so students go to war zone.

text.p: Khartoum University has closed so that students can join the forces and go to eastern Sudan to counter what Sudan says are Ethiopian attacks at the border.

State radio quoted a university official on Tuesday as saying classes had been suspended "to allow students to join popular defence forces on their way to eastern Sudan to fight Ethiopian aggression".
It said the classes were suspended at all faculties at the university, the oldest of several in Khartoum. It did not say how many students had joined the government call to mobilise.
The radio announcement was the latest call by the Islamist government to prepare the public for a military campaign after the army said on Monday that Ethiopian forces had attacked two border towns.
Sudan's armed forces have said Ethiopian forces, along with what they called "remnants of agents and mercenaries", shelled the towns of Kurmuk and Qassein.
President Omar Hassan al-Bashir has called for "general mobilisation" against the threat but the government has not announced any specific compulsory measures.
On Monday the radio said that a brigade of the paramilitary People's Defence Forces was preparing to leave Khartoum towards the towns, about 600 km (370 miles) southeast of the capital.

In Eritrea on Tuesday, the Sudan People's Liberation Army said a joint rebel force had captured key Sudanese government army garrisons at Al-Kali, Daimonsour and Shali al-Fil in the southern Blue Nile region.
Its spokesman in Asmara, Yassir Arman, told Reuters the operation was carried out on Monday by a joint force of the umbrella opposition group, the National Democratic Alliance.
